seoTitle: Typeform vs Jotform: Which Form Builder Wins in 2026
metaDescription: Typeform vs Jotform compared on form style, AI features, integrations and 2026 pricing: responses, form caps and when each removes its branding.
intro:
Typeform and Jotform both collect answers through online forms, but they meter you differently, and that difference decides the cost more than any feature list. Typeform gives you unlimited forms on every paid plan and counts responses. Jotform counts both: a cap on how many forms you can have and a cap on monthly submissions.

This comparison covers Jotform's pitch against Typeform, what each workspace looks like, how form styles differ, integrations, and the September 2026 plan limits side by side.

steps.heading: Jotform markets directly against Typeform
steps.body: Jotform runs a whole landing page headed "The Smart Alternative to Typeform. More Features, More Power." It claims conditional logic on every plan including free, 24/7 support, a free mobile app, free access to all its integrations, and Jotform Cards, its own one-question-at-a-time format. The listed features are real. Still, read it as a competitor's sales page. It says nothing about Jotform's per-plan form caps, which is where Typeform has the edge.

image.caption: Jotform's own "Typeform Alternative" landing page, pitching more features and a stronger free plan directly against Typeform.

steps.heading: Compare the workspaces, not only the pitch
steps.body: Typeform's My workspace puts AI-suggested templates at the top, cards like "Monitor project milestones" with a one-click Use this form button, next to a counter of free responses left this month. It steers you towards one next step. Jotform's workspace shows more options at once and expects more configuration up front. Coming from one to the other, you'll find the second either refreshingly simple or frustratingly bare.

image.caption: Typeform's workspace with AI-suggested form templates and a free-tier response counter, open alongside Jotform tabs for a side-by-side comparison.

steps.heading: One question at a time, or the whole form at once
steps.body:
Typeform's signature is one question per screen in a full-screen flow. That format is why people pick it for quizzes, lead forms and anything customer-facing where the feel matters, and it's the default for every form you build there.

Jotform does both. Its classic forms show many fields on a page, which suits long intake forms and applications, and Jotform Cards gives a Typeform-style one-question flow. So the question isn't which format each tool supports. It's which one each tool is built around.

steps.heading: AI features
steps.body: Typeform lists AI-powered form creation from its Basic plan up, and its workspace surfaces AI-suggested templates. The Growth Flow plan adds Smart Insights for analysing responses. Jotform's AI centres on Jotform AI for building forms from a prompt and on AI Agents, conversational assistants whose usage is metered per plan (the free Starter plan includes 5 active agents and 100 conversations a month). If you only want help drafting questions, both cover it. If you want a chatbot-style assistant attached to your forms, that's Jotform's territory.

steps.heading: Integrations run in different directions
steps.body: Typeform's integration browser covers the usual lead-generation and survey stack: HubSpot and Pipedrive for CRM, Google Sheets and Notion for data, Mailchimp and Slack for notifications, Stripe for payments. It's filterable by categories like Marketing automation and Payments & e-commerce. Jotform says all its integrations are free on every plan. It also leans on its own products, including Jotform Tables, Jotform Sign for e-signatures, a PDF editor and built-in payment fields, so more of the workflow stays inside Jotform.

image.caption: Typeform's Popular integrations browser, filterable by category, showing HubSpot, Google Sheets, Calendly, Mailchimp, and dozens more connected apps.

steps.heading: Choosing between them
steps.body: Pick Typeform when the form is part of the brand experience and you run many small forms. Unlimited forms suit that, as long as total responses stay within your tier. Pick Jotform when you need more submissions per dollar, long multi-field forms, e-signatures or PDFs, or HIPAA features (Gold and above). Watch the form cap if you build lots of one-off forms. Some teams run both: Typeform for short branded lead forms, Jotform for long internal ones.

faq.question: Which has the better free plan?
faq.answer: For volume, Jotform. Its Starter plan allows 100 submissions a month across up to 5 forms, while the Typeform free workspace in the recording counted 10 responses a month. Both free plans show the vendor's branding.

faq.question: Does Jotform limit how many forms I can create?
faq.answer: Yes. Starter allows 5, Bronze 25, Silver 50 and Gold 100. Typeform's paid plans have no form limit and meter responses instead.

faq.question: Can Jotform do one-question-at-a-time forms like Typeform?
faq.answer: Yes, with Jotform Cards. You choose between the classic multi-field layout and Cards when you build the form.

faq.question: When can I remove the branding?
faq.answer: On Jotform, on any paid plan from Bronze. On Typeform, from the Plus plan; Basic still shows Typeform branding.

faq.question: Is Jotform's "Typeform Alternative" page a fair comparison?
faq.answer: The features it lists are real, but it's a competitor's marketing page. It leaves out Jotform's form caps, so check both pricing pages against your expected monthly volume and number of forms.
